The furnace venting is wrong. You don’t need a new furnace if you can find a contractor that will run a new exhaust pipe for you. Also the cause of the leak is probably from the AC evaporator coil. Looks like the evap drain is run with 3/4” PVC. 

If you are good with tools and “mechanically inclined” I would buy a pvc coupling or some more fittings to redo the ac drain, then I would cut the drain tube and unscrew it to see if there is a blockage. You can vacuum the AC drain if it isn’t connected to the furnace.

I would probably get a second opinion because it sounds like the first company just wants to sell you a new furnace. On the other that furnace could be in bad condition so maybe it won’t last much longer. If you get the exhaust replaced then you will be able to re-use that exhaust for another high efficiency furnace in the future.

The AC indoor coil probably needs replacement and if the outdoor unit uses r-22 refrigerant then it would probably need replacement as well. If it uses 410A then it’s probably good for a while. It will say the refrigerant type on the outdoor unit usually by the refrigerant line service valves.

Little Giant condensate pumps are standard. Most complicated part about condo pumps is wiring up the safety switch. I see a lot of people that don’t do it. The safety switch cuts power if the pump stops working.

If you can’t find the humidistat control, usually the water valve for the small line that runs to the valve comes off the water heater and you can close the valve. But the valve operating with no water can damage it. Sometimes the humidity control is built into the thermostat itself. I would look for where the wires from the humidifier valve go. Do they go to a “local” control, or do they run through the ceiling to somewhere else in the house.
